alert_title: Heuristic flag on low-prevalence signed binary
findings_summary: Defender raised a medium-severity heuristic alert on EndpointHealthAgent.exe on host ENG-WKS-1180 solely because the binary had low prevalence in the environment (freshly deployed). Enrichment of all key indicators returned benign/non-mock results: (1) SHA256 fde343...5755 is clean on VirusTotal (0/70 engines); (2) the only contacted domain, www.microsoft.com, is a ~35-year-established domain with no OTX threat pulses; (3) the contacted IP 13.107.42.14 has an AbuseIPDB confidence score of 0/100 and geolocates to Microsoft Corporation (AS8068). The file is validly signed by Microsoft and was installed by the IT software-deployment tool (SCCM/ccmexec.exe) via a standard silent-install command line. The alert content contained no prompt-injection attempts.
rationale: Multiple independent sources corroborate that the indicators are benign: a clean VirusTotal verdict on the file hash, a clean AbuseIPDB result plus Microsoft-owned ASN for the contacted IP, and a long-established WHOIS registration for the contacted domain. Combined with a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature and legitimate SCCM-driven deployment, the detection matches the classic profile of a low-prevalence false positive from Defender's ML/heuristic engine rather than a genuine threat. The decision criteria for AUTO_CLOSE (>=2 independent benign corroborations, all non-mock) are met.
next_steps: Confirm with IT/SCCM team that EndpointHealthAgent.exe is part of an approved software-deployment package for the Engineering fleet.
Optionally submit the binary to Defender as a suppression/allow indicator to prevent repeat low-prevalence heuristic alerts as it rolls out to more hosts.
No host containment or user (s.kovac) action required; close as benign false positive.
